newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen halting 11-session rise.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen halting 11-session rise.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa was seen soft at the opening Tuesday after an 11-session climb as stocks come under pressure from the U.S. Treasuries market, dealers said.

"New York was shocked by a strong confidence report early today, pushing the long bond yield over the key level of 7.0 percent. This is likely to cause a correction here after such a long climb," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
The blue-chip MerVal index added 0.2 percent to 768.92 Monday. It had advanced 6.2 percent in the previous two weeks without recording a single loss.

"Today it looks like we're tilting lower but I don't expect any major sell-off," another dealer said. "The market still wants to rise based on news like strong industrial production growth and today's merger between Banco Rio de la Plata and Banco Santander, which is keeping Argentine bank stocks firm in New York."

Spain's Santander announced Tuesday it would purchase 35.1 percent of Banco Rio and take control of the local bank. The deal was announced two weeks after Banco Frances said it would acquire Banco de Credito Argentino.
